Anything that greps specs/ISO_COBOL.md for normative language — the spec-lookup skill, a citation check, a human reading the file — will hit first-person assistant prose sitting inside ISO/IEC 1989:2023. It also marks the page as knowingly incomplete, so any future "the spec does not say X" conclusion drawn from page 28 is unsound. Verified with grep over the whole file: these two lines occur exactly once, at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 1255 and 1281, both inside the page-28 slice — the contamination is confined to this page.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim if anything understates the defect. PDF side: rendered page 28 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v28/spec_p28.png) and read the image directly. The page is a normal, fully legible printed ISO page: running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'; the heading 'Introduction'; nine body paragraphs plus a three-item dashed list (FLOW-MATIC(TM)1; IBM(R)2 Commercial Translator Form No F 28-8013, copyrighted 1959 by IBM; FACT(C), DSI 27A5260-2760, copyrighted 1960 by Minneapolis-Honeywell); two numbered trademark footnotes (Sperry Rand / IBM); the footer 'xxviii (C)ISO/IEC 2023'; and the per-copy license watermark line. There is no first-person prose, no summary framing, and no refusal text anywhere on the page. The claim's characterization of the PDF page is accurate (it omits only the license watermark line, which is immaterial). Markdown side: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 1255 reads exactly 'Here is a summary and key excerpts from this page of ISO/IEC 1989:2023(E):' and line 1281 reads exactly 'I can quote specific short passages if needed, but I'm not able to reproduce the full page verbatim as a complete copyrighted standards document. I'm happy to help you find specific information from this page.' Both sit between the ' / ## Page 28' anchor at line 1253 and the '' anchor at line 1283, i.e. inside the page-28 slice. grep confirms each string occurs exactly once in the file, so the contamination is confined to page 28 as claimed. The claim does not misquote either source. This is not page-break furniture, reflow, hyphenation, or formatting: the meta-text has no counterpart in the PDF at all, and it changes what the file asserts about itself. Escalating detail found while verifying: the two flagged lines are only the frame. The 26 lines of the page-28 slice contain ZERO verbatim spec text — the entire body is a third-person paraphrase ('The introduction explains that...', 'It includes reproduction permissions...', 'The page notes that...'). I grepped the whole 48k+ line file for four distinctive page-28 sentences and got zero hits for every one: 'interested in reproducing the COBOL standard' (0), 'not the property of any company or group of companies' (0), 'Sperry Rand' (0, both footnotes absent), and the sentence 'For more details and additional changes, see E.2, Substantive changes potentially affecting existing programs and E.3, Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs.' (0 — the E.2 hits at lines 1090/4414/48524/48906 are the TOC entry, an unrelated NOTE in the body, and Annex E itself, not this sentence). So 100% of page 28's printed body text is missing from the transcription, not merely bracketed by meta-text.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but the described scope is too narrow. The claim is factually correct as far as it goes — lines 1255 and 1281 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md are transcription-tool meta-text and an assistant refusal message embedded inside the page-28 slice, they occur exactly once each in the file, and nothing resembling them appears on the rendered PDF page. Severity 'structural' is right. The correction is to the extent: those two lines are not stray insertions around an otherwise-good transcription — they bracket a paraphrase that replaces the page entirely. Every one of the 26 lines between the page-28 and page-29 anchors is summary prose; not a single sentence of the printed Introduction body survives verbatim. Confirmed absent from the entire file: the reproduction-permission paragraph ('Any organization interested in reproducing the COBOL standard and specifications in whole or in part... requested to mention "COBOL" in acknowledgment of the source'), the industry-language paragraph ('COBOL is an industry language and is not the property of any company or group of companies, or of any organization or group of organizations.'), the no-warranty paragraph, the cross-reference sentence 'For more details and additional changes, see E.2, Substantive changes potentially affecting existing programs and E.3, Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs.', the exact Annex-normativity sentence naming Annexes A/B/C by title, and both trademark footnotes (Sperry Rand, IBM). The remediation is therefore a full re-transcription of page 28 from the render, not a two-line deletion — deleting lines 1255 and 1281 alone would leave a paraphrase masquerading as a transcription and would remove the only marker that the page is incomplete.
